assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correction of spherical aberration in electron lenses turned transmission electron microscopy into a routine sub-angstrom, quantitative tool, enabling atomic-column imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects, oxides and nanoparticles across physics, materials science and chemistry. It is a clear invention with a concrete instrument realization and very broad, lasting impact. I assess it from within the field, so I weigh it as a discovery-or-invention case rather than a lifetime achievement.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names map naturally onto the decisive steps: Rose on the aberration-corrector theory and design, Haider on the hexapole corrector realization for the TEM, and Urban on the demonstration and use for atomic-resolution materials imaging. Credit among the wider group (e.g. other collaborators on the first implementations) is not fully resolved by the supplied text, but the three-person configuration is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Correctors have been commercially available and used in thousands of laboratories for roughly two decades; confirmation is independent and extensive, and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would regard a microscopy instrument invention as physics rather than a methods or chemistry prize.
Exact division of credit between theory of the corrector and its first working realization is from memory and not verified here.
I have a professional closeness to the electron-microscopy community, which should be flagged as a possible bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a new and highly productive platform for strongly correlated and topological phases with tunable parameters. Originality and impact are high, with a clean prediction-to-experiment story.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states. The supplied credit supports a theory plus experiment configuration. Other experimental contributors and earlier moire theory could be argued for, which complicates a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups since 2018 and extended to many moire systems, but some interpretation of the superconducting mechanism and the full phase diagram is still evolving, so the field is young.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and phase-diagram interpretation remain debated.
Priority questions about earlier twisted-graphene theory and the role of other experimental groups are not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of the magic-wavelength optical lattice and its realization in clocks reaching fractional uncertainties of 1e-18 gave a new basis for time and frequency, with consequences for tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. This is a precise, well-defined invention with substantial lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the original magic-wavelength lattice-clock proposal and early realizations; Jun Ye brought the clock to record accuracy and many-body-clock regimes. Two names give a fair and compact configuration, though other groups (e.g. strontium and ytterbium efforts elsewhere) also contributed and credit is not wholly clean.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories have confirmed the performance; the second redefinition process is underway but not complete, so some of the practical payoff is still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock recognition may make a committee reluctant.
Credit to other groups and to the closely related ion-clock work is not resolved by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuinely new type of semiconductor laser based on engineered intersubband transitions in layered heterostructures, with design freedom across the mid-infrared and terahertz. It is a clear invention with wide technological and scientific use in spectroscopy and sensing, resting on molecular-beam-epitaxy materials control.
assessment.attribution: Capasso led the Bell Labs concept and team, Faist carried out the first demonstration in 1994, and Cho supplied the epitaxial growth capability. Other Bell Labs co-authors on the first device exist and the weight given to the growth contribution relative to the concept is a matter of judgment, but a trio is defensible.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent development, with room-temperature continuous-wave operation and commercial devices; recognition is timely to overdue.
uncertainties: Other co-inventors of the first device are not among the supplied names.
Whether the committee sees the laser as device engineering versus discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, established a new class of materials defined by topology and protected edge or surface states. Conceptual importance is very high and the field has had far-reaching effects.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the Z2 and quantum spin Hall predictions; Molenkamp led the HgTe experiment. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal and the three-dimensional topological insulator work are not among the supplied names, so the credit is incomplete and contested in a way the longlist entry does not settle.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by independent experiments including three-dimensional materials and ARPES; recognition is mature, although some applications remain prospective.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit for the HgTe proposal and 3D topological insulators, and overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize.
Supplied names may not support the fairest configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realized controllable Hubbard models, shown first by the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and later by single-site imaging of correlated states, giving a quantum simulator for many-body physics. It is a major conceptual and technical advance, though a compound one.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch supplied the theoretical proposal, Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition and microscopy work, and Esslinger the fermionic realization. Choosing three from the four supplied names is hard, and I would favour a configuration that mixes theory and experiment, but this is an arguable cut.
assessment.maturity: Many confirmations and a mature subfield, though the application-level claim of useful simulation beyond classical reach is still developing.
uncertainties: Compound discovery whose strands could need different recognition.
Allocation among Zoller, Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger is unresolved, and overlap with 2001 and 2012 atomic-physics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskites reached high photovoltaic efficiency very rapidly with solution processing, and their defect tolerance and optoelectronic properties raised fundamental physics questions. Impact is large, but a good share of the work is in chemistry and materials engineering, and the physical understanding is incomplete.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites in sensitized solar cells, Park made the solid-state cell with improved stability and efficiency, and Snaith demonstrated high-efficiency thin-film devices. The three-person configuration is plausible, though credit disputes with other groups are known to me, not resolved by the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced worldwide, but long-term stability and commercialization are not settled, so recognition may be premature for a physics prize.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial maturity are uncertain.
Fit to physics rather than chemistry or applied energy research.
Credit disputes over early efficiency milestones.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state quantum system used for nanoscale magnetic, electric and thermal sensing. It is an original and widely applied result with clear relevance to materials characterization.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko did the foundational single-centre detection and coherent spin control; Lukin and others contributed a large body of later quantum-information and sensing work, but a two-person prize on the early discovery is cleaner and consistent with the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and the basis of an active sensing field, though the more ambitious quantum-network and sensing applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the foundational discovery or later sensing applications would be the prize topic.
Credit to Lukin and to earlier ensemble NV work is not decided from the supplied names.
